description: Two squadrons, one command, and the kind always comes first. Launched mining drones pick their own rocks - nearest ore or ice inside the ship's drone control range, recalling themselves when the hold fills or one of them takes fire - and launched salvage drones work the wrecks around the ship, nearest first or farthest first, going home when the cargo hold fills. /aud m is the mining menu (on/off, spread/focus, range, threshold, control, filter, list, status); /aud s is the salvage one (on/off, spread/focus, distance, foreign, range, threshold, list, status), and /aud on its own prints the two menus without guessing which was meant. A wreck that belongs to somebody else is only touched when the pilot says so: "foreign warn" works it and prints one warning line per launch, "foreign allow" works it silently, and "foreign off" - the default - leaves it alone. The game's own loot entitlement and the pilot's safety light still decide whether anything may move at all, and a wreck the light refuses is skipped with a warning. The mining queue is a priority list printed as one numbered list per kind of rock, a mistyped rock name is answered with the one it meant, and /aud copy hands one character's whole setup to another, which is what a multibox fleet wants. Both kinds are classified by the game's own drone effects, so a hull that launches fifty drones under a third-party mod works them all. Every character drives it from ordinary chat (!aud), so no staff rights are needed, and what they choose is saved per character. Server-side only; no client change.
